content: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures, known in French as the Bureau international des poids et mesures (BIPM), is an international standards organization. It is one of three organizations established to oversee the International System of Units (SI) under the terms of the Metre Convention, a diplomatic treaty. The BIPM is headquartered at the Pavillon de Breteuil in Sèvres, France, where it enjoys extraterritorial status. This unique status allowed it to avoid German occupation during World War II. The BIPM plays a critical role in ensuring the uniformity of SI units of measurement across the globe. It operates under the authority of the Metre Convention, which, as of 2005, includes 51 member nations. The organization achieves its objectives through a network of Consultative Committees, whose members are the national metrology laboratories of the Convention's member states, as well as through its own laboratory research and activities. The BIPM conducts research related to measurement science and participates in organizing international comparisons of national measurement standards. It also provides calibration services for its member states. Furthermore, the BIPM has a significant role in maintaining accurate global timekeeping. It combines, analyzes, and averages the official atomic time standards from member nations to produce a unified and official Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
